bad.title: Advanced is a second form
bad.text: Switching shows other fields, not the ones people just filled in.

bad.title: From is empty again
bad.text: Lisbon and the To city are gone, so people type the trip twice.

bad.title: Search reads only one form
bad.text: Results depend on which mode people last had open.

good.title: Advanced only adds fields
good.text: Switching keeps everything people already typed.

good.title: One From, one To
good.text: Both modes share these fields, so their values can’t drift apart.

good.title: The extras slot in below
good.text: Return, Cabin and Direct flights only, under the same From and To.
good.wait: Switch to Advanced to see this.

bad.title: An unlabeled icon in the corner
bad.text: Nothing says it holds filters, so people scroll the list instead.

bad.title: Six shirts to scan by eye
bad.text: People read every size line to find the ones in M.

good.title: A named button, in the open
good.text: It lists size, color and price before anyone presses it.

good.title: Size M in two clicks
good.text: The list drops to the 3 shirts that come in M.

bad.title: Warmth still tints the photo
bad.text: The Advanced change stays on, so the photo looks off for no clear reason.

bad.title: Simple shows only the looks
bad.text: Original, Vivid and Mono, and no trace of Warmth to undo.

good.title: Names the hidden change
good.text: “1 advanced setting changed: warmth” explains the warm tint.
good.wait: Raise Warmth in Advanced, then go back to Simple, to see this.

good.title: Show jumps to the slider
good.text: People land on Warmth in Advanced, ready to adjust it.
good.wait: Raise Warmth in Advanced, then go back to Simple, to see this.

good.title: Reset without leaving Simple
good.text: One click puts Contrast and Warmth back to their defaults.
good.wait: Raise Warmth in Advanced, then go back to Simple, to see this.

bad.title: Simple has no Out-of-office
bad.text: People look here first and find only Name, Theme and Language.

bad.title: Eleven settings, in no order
bad.text: Expert switches and everyday ones share one unsorted list.
bad.wait: Switch to Advanced to see this.

bad.title: Out-of-office reply, tenth down
bad.text: A setting many people need, found only after a long scan.
bad.wait: Switch to Advanced to see this.

good.title: Out-of-office reply in Simple
good.text: It’s where people look first, one click from the top.

good.title: Advanced is short and grouped
good.text: Five settings, under Sending and Your data.
good.wait: Switch to Advanced to see this.

good.title: A default replaced an option
good.text: Links are always converted, so nobody has to hunt for that switch.
good.wait: Switch to Advanced to see this.

bad.title: Next, with no key shown
bad.text: N skips a song, but nothing on screen says so.

bad.title: No list of keys anywhere
bad.text: There’s no Shortcuts button or “?” to look them up.

bad.title: With keys stays at 0
bad.text: People keep clicking, because they never learn the faster way.

good.title: N sits right on Next
good.text: People see the key every time they click, and pick it up.

good.title: Shortcuts, with ? beside it
good.text: The full list is one click or one key away.

good.title: Every key in one list
good.text: Next, Previous, Like, and ? for the list itself.

bad.title: Ctrl+W already closes tabs
bad.text: In a real browser, the tab closes before the app sees the key.

bad.title: The whole tab is gone
bad.text: Weather is showing, and the note’s last changes are lost.
bad.wait: Press Ctrl + W to see this.

good.title: Esc, a key the browser leaves free
good.text: Close note works, and Ctrl+W still closes tabs as people expect.

good.title: Every key in one place
good.text: Shortcuts lists Close note, New note and Search notes together.

good.title: Each key can be changed
good.text: People can switch to Alt+Q or Ctrl+Alt+W if Esc gets in their way.

bad.title: A archives, wherever focus is
bad.text: Nothing limits the key to the message list.

bad.title: The first “a” archives the chat
bad.text: “Thanks” stops at “Th”, and the reply is lost with the chat.

good.title: A works in the message list
good.text: Esc leaves the reply box, and then A archives.

good.title: Letters stay letters here
good.text: People can type “Thanks, see you at 6” in full.

bad.title: No Duplicate in the menu
bad.text: Only Edit and Delete, so people on a mouse or touch screen can’t copy Yoga.
bad.wait: Pick Yoga and press ⋯ to see this.

bad.title: Tuesday stays empty
bad.text: Without the D key, the only way is to make the class again by hand.

good.title: Duplicate in the ⋯ menu
good.text: A visible path for people who never use the keyboard.
good.wait: Pick Yoga and press ⋯ to see this.

good.title: D shown beside it
good.text: The menu teaches the faster key along the way.
good.wait: Pick Yoga and press ⋯ to see this.

bad.title: Offers lead the home screen
bad.text: The first thing people see is a sales pitch, not their money.

bad.title: Balance and Pay sit below the fold
bad.text: People scroll past three cards for the thing they opened the app for.

bad.title: Customize can’t rescue it
bad.text: Most people never open it, so the weak default is what they get.

good.title: Balance and Pay at the top
good.text: €2,340.50 and Pay are the first thing people see.

good.title: Recent payments come next
good.text: Rent and the grocer, what people check right after the balance.

good.title: Customize stays for the rest
good.text: People who want offers first can still move them up.

bad.title: Mum stays in the plain list
bad.text: After three shares she’s still fifth of seven, and nothing offers to help.

bad.title: Favorites hide in Settings
bad.text: The only way in is Settings › Sharing, far from the share sheet.
bad.wait: Share with Mum three times to see this.

good.title: The offer comes at the third share
good.text: “Add to favorites?” shows up right where people are sharing.
good.wait: Share with Mum three times to see this.

good.title: Not now ends it for good
good.text: It won’t ask about Mum again, so the offer never nags.

good.title: Mum moves to the top
good.text: She sits under Favorites, one click away next time.
good.wait: Share with Mum three times and press Add to see this.

bad.title: The help says “the third item”
bad.text: It was written for the default order, where the third item is Privacy.

bad.title: Display jumps to the top
bad.text: Privacy slides to fourth, so the help now leads to Notifications.

good.title: The help note stays true
good.text: The third item is still Privacy, whatever people pin.

good.title: Pins get their own row
good.text: Display shows up top and also keeps its place in the list.

good.title: Reset to default, in plain sight
good.text: One button clears every pin.

bad.title: 6 pinned, and growing
bad.text: Pinned is already three times longer than Recent.

bad.title: No way to unpin from the row
bad.text: People open the chat, then Chat info, then Unpin, for every pin.

good.title: Unpin right on the row
good.text: One click per chat, without leaving the list.

good.title: An empty state that teaches
good.text: With no pins left, it says what pins are for and how they behave.
good.wait: Unpin all six chats to see this.
